taxonomy_mapping_dispositions.reason: The chatbot presented an incorrect bereavement-fare rule as usable Air Canada policy on a customer-service surface, and the passenger relied on it for a consequential fare decision. The generated policy statement did not meet the factual and policy-fidelity assurance threshold required for that downstream reliance.

dimensions.assessment_basis: No separately bandable materialised impact in this dimension is established beyond the occurrence-specific assessment.

The Civil Resolution Tribunal ordered Air Canada to pay C$650.88 in damages, C$36.14 interest and C$125 in fees, totalling C$812.02. The Bank of Canada decision-date rate of US$0.7380 per C$1 converts that total to US$599.27, below USD 10,000 and without evidence of livelihood or organisational-viability impairment. Threshold applied: Aggregate direct realised loss below USD 10,000, provided the evidence does not establish material livelihood or organisational-viability impairment.

The tribunal determined C$650.88 as the fare difference caused by reliance on the chatbot. It separately awarded C$36.14 interest and C$125 fees, totalling C$812.02. The historically sourced 14 February 2024 Bank of Canada rate of US$0.7380 per C$1 places even that total at US$599.27. The award is not proof of payment or the whole sum being underlying fare loss. The adjudicated fare/resource burden is below US$10,000 and no material livelihood impairment is evidenced. The alternative S2 low-disruption and S3 material-livelihood criteria are considered; neither overrides the defensible small USD quantum and absence of a reported qualifying livelihood consequence.
